corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Jump distinguishes reality from mind-dependent sentences, using tree analogy to explain how descriptions represent objective conditions without transcendent existence, thereby answering Settecase’s connective-principle challenge through an ontological reframe. Principal limitation: Equating propositions with sentences remains undefended, because linguistic dependence establishes neither the nonexistence of abstract truth-contents nor the subjectivity of modal relations, so the analogy understates a charitable interpretation. Live burden: Jump must substantiate his linguistic account while explaining how logical necessity, normativity, and counterfactual validity emerge from mind-dependent formulations without conflating expressions, contents, and realities. Locked score: Exceptional responsiveness and burden contact support the competent band, while overstated certainty, implicit qualification, moderate warrant, and limited representational charity appropriately constrain the assessment to 81.
